questions.q: Why does the chapter say you cannot simply stop when you arrive?
options: Because the body sits but the mind keeps running, so unprepared people spend Day 1 coming down from speed
Because the retreat schedule is too demanding
Because God only speaks on Day 3
Because silence is impossible without training
questions.explanation: Psalm 131 describes the destination, a calmed and quieted soul, and the verb is active. The psalmist did not arrive there by accident.

questions.q: What does the ten-minute practice for the week before consist of?
options: An hour of Bible study and a written summary
Read a psalm twice, sit quietly for up to three minutes, pray one sentence about the retreat
Fast from one meal each day
Listen to a sermon and take notes
questions.explanation: The purpose is attention, not endurance: a small, familiar path into quiet, and a chance to notice how your mind and body respond.

questions.q: How does the chapter tell you to treat resistance that appears in the week before?
options: As a sign you should cancel
As spiritual attack to be pushed through
As information, not a command: ask what it might be telling you
As proof the retreat is self-indulgent
questions.explanation: It may be ordinary reluctance, fear of what may surface, a practical problem, or a genuine safety concern. Respond to what you discover rather than dramatising every hesitation.

questions.q: In Matthew 5:23–24, who is Jesus speaking about when he says to go and be reconciled first?
options: Everyone who has ever wronged you
Only members of your own family
Your pastor
A person who has something against you, a wrong you have done
questions.explanation: He is not instructing you to chase reconciliation with everyone who has hurt you, and you are not required to contact someone unsafe. Forgiveness and reconciliation are not the same thing.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about confession before the retreat?
options: Confess what you already know and leave the rest to God; do not turn it into a search
Comb your life for hidden sins to explain your dryness
Wait until Session Five for all confession
Confession is unnecessary before a retreat
questions.explanation: 1 John 1:9 gives the promise plainly. If you find yourself confessing the same matter repeatedly because you cannot feel forgiven, speak with a pastor or professional who understands scrupulosity.

options: Cancelling all your responsibilities
Writing down what needs doing and who is doing it, routing urgent contact through one person, and giving the person covering clear authority
Telling no one you are leaving
Checking in with everyone daily
questions.explanation: Jethro told Moses that carrying everything alone was 'not good' (Exodus 18). A poorly handed-over responsibility follows you into the retreat as a low hum of worry.

reflection: Which day this week will you begin the ten-minute practice? Write the time and the place.
What resistance have you already noticed? Write down, without analysing it, what you think it may be telling you.

Is there a relationship or a known sin that Matthew 5 or 1 John 1 applies to, one you can and should address before you go? If yes, what will you do and when? If no, or if it is not safe, write that down.
Who will you ask to pray for you, and what exactly will you say?
